newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Sammi Steel defaults on loans.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Sammi Steel defaults on loans.

text.p: South Korea's troubled Sammi Steel Co on Wednesday defaulted on payments of promissory notes worth about 1.8 billion won, creditor banks said.
Dongnam Bank said Sammi failed to pay 687 million won of notes today on top of 849 million won on Tuesday.
SEOUL Bank also said the steel maker could not pay 270 million won until today's deadline. The money was supposed to be repaid by Tuesday.
Sammi Steel Co sought protection from its creditors on Tuesday along with four other affiliates of Sammi Group, South Korea's 26th largest conglomerate.
In January, Hanbo Steel filed for receivership under debts of $5.8 billion in South Korea's biggest corporate collapse.
Hanbo's bankruptcy had made it more difficult for Sammi to obtain fresh loans.
"We had more difficulty negotiating for fresh loans with financial institutions after the Hanbo scandal broke," said one Sammi executive, who declined to be identified.
A Dongnam Bank official said Sammi's bank transactions would not be frozen if the company came up with money by Thursday morning.
"But the possibility looks slim because the Korea First Bank, Sammi's prime bank, declared it would not supply additional funds to the troubled company," the official said.
Sammi Steel had liabilities of 1.45 trillion won at the end of 1996 against assets of 1.53 trillion won, according to company figures.
